items.proposal: Use fixed 75% soft and 80% hard thresholds.
items.risk: Thresholds are unvalidated and provider/model/tokenizer dependent.
items.required_control: Measured tokenizer-bound budget policy and post-reconstruction budget assertion.

items.proposal: Estimate tokens from characters divided by 3.5.
items.risk: Language, tokenizer, tool payload and provider accounting make this non-exact.
items.required_control: Provider tokenizer or billed usage readback with declared tolerance.

items.proposal: An in-memory dictionary acts as VFS persistence.
items.risk: It is not durable, concurrent, encrypted, tenant-isolated, recoverable or versioned.
items.required_control: Crash/fault/recovery matrix over a durable versioned store.

items.proposal: Moving a cut point past tool-role messages preserves tool-call atomicity.
items.risk: The assistant tool-call message and ordered one-to-many results can still be split or reordered.
items.required_control: Transaction graph with stable IDs, cardinality and safe-boundary assertion.

items.risk: Capabilities are provider-specific; hidden reasoning may be inaccessible and must not be requested.
items.required_control: Exact provider capability matrix and visible sync-point controls.

items.proposal: NLI/Judge and repair produce zero-hallucination reports.
items.risk: Probabilistic semantic checks can abstain, conflict or fail and cannot guarantee truth.
items.required_control: Independent evidence lanes, abstention/conflict states and Human review.

items.proposal: A permissive SPDX whitelist establishes commercial safety.
items.risk: Dependencies, custom terms, model/data/trace rights, privacy and ToS require separate review.
items.required_control: Exact four-dimensional provenance and Human legal/security review.

items.proposal: AST slicing plus LLM reimplementation creates clean-room closure.
items.risk: Technical rewriting does not itself establish legal independence or prevent copied restricted bytes.
items.required_control: Independent behavior specification, provenance separation and Human policy/legal decision.

items.risk: Sanitizer order, exporter routes, logs, retention, RBAC and network egress remain unproven.
items.required_control: Sanitize-before-export data-flow and negative leak controls.

items.proposal: FastAPI BackgroundTasks provides asynchronous workflow dispatch.
items.risk: A process crash can lose work after HTTP 202; no durable inbox/outbox, backpressure or DLQ exists.
items.required_control: Transactional durable queue with restart/replay and duplicate controls.

items.proposal: Generic token/HMAC examples cover GitLab/Jira webhook security.
items.risk: Provider semantics, replay windows, secret defaults and event schemas are oversimplified.
items.required_control: Provider-specific auth/replay contract and planted signature/replay failures.

items.proposal: Path, line and Python AST checks make code-trace hallucination zero.
items.risk: Commit/tree, symlink, exact snippet, parser coverage and syntax-error handling are missing.
items.required_control: Exact-subject readback with normalized path, snippet digest, parser identity and unsupported state.

items.proposal: Docker bridge mode and resource limits provide a safe sandbox.
items.risk: Bridge networking is not zero egress; shell clone, mounts, privilege and cleanup require hardening.
items.required_control: Default-deny runtime profile and negative isolation/residue canary.

items.proposal: A passed Gate can write back or close the workflow.
items.risk: Task success, external effect, user outcome, Human admission, merge and release are separate evidence states.
items.required_control: Lane-literal receipts and Human-owned terminal transitions.
